modelNote: A whole-county cooperative has to reach four payment groups, and they differ in exactly ONE variable: who holds the money and what they are permitted to buy with it. The order, the care teams, the verification, the microcommunity and the catalytic test are identical in all four. So this is not four designs — it is one workbench with four purchaser adapters. The strongest consequence is at the bottom: because the plan belongs to the person rather than to the payer, it survives a change of payer. Drawn Aug 17 2026.

nodes.label: The four groups differ in ONE variable: who holds the money. Everything to the right of the adapters is identical in all four.
nodes.note: This is why the design is one workbench rather than four. The order, the care teams, the verification, the microcommunity, the catalytic test and the safety ramp do not change when the payer changes. Only the adapter does.

nodes.label: EMPLOYERS
nodes.note: Self-funded employers and their employees. Roughly half the county at most — which is why the employer route alone cannot make this a whole-county cooperative.

nodes.label: MEDICARE
nodes.note: The money is federal (CMS). Whatcom skews older, so this group is large here — and it is the group for whom continuity of a plan matters most.

nodes.label: MEDICAID
nodes.note: Apple Health in Washington: the state contracts managed care organisations, and the region has an Accountable Community of Health. Low rates, but the only payer that already buys community health workers, care coordination and some housing support.

nodes.label: THE UNINSURED
nodes.note: There is no premium at all, so the counterparty lever the whole design rests on is simply absent. What exists instead is AVOIDED COST — money someone is already spending on emergency care, plus hospital community-benefit dollars that must be spent anyway.

nodes.label: CONTRACT AS AGENT for a pool of self-funded employers
nodes.note: The counterparty seat without an insurance licence. Needs a pool, a settlement rail or third-party administrator, stop-loss cover, and a health lawyer before instruments are drafted. Detailed in Appendix A — it is the first adapter because it needs nobody's permission.

nodes.label: AN ACO — accountable care organisation
nodes.note: Already the shape we designed: an attributed panel, a spending benchmark, shared savings, quality measures — and no insurance licence. Medicare arrives with risk adjustment built in, which the money design requires anyway.

nodes.label: DELEGATED ARRANGEMENT with a managed care organisation, or the regional ACH
nodes.note: Subcontract to take delegated responsibility for a population, or work through the Accountable Community of Health. This is the best first payer for the PLACE register, because it is the only one that already buys the social layer.

nodes.label: AVOIDED COST — hospital community benefit, county funds, a low-cost membership
nodes.note: The counterparty here is the hospital and the county rather than an employer. A hospital would rather fund a CHW team than absorb the emergency visits, and community benefit is money it is obliged to spend regardless. The membership product is a club good — see the sorting frame.

nodes.label: Employers can leave the pool after one bad year — and the pool is the leverage
nodes.note: Which is why stop-loss cover is not a technicality: it buys the experiment enough time to show anything.

nodes.label: Benchmark ratcheting: beat the target and next year's target drops
nodes.note: Succeed and you are rewarded with a harder benchmark. That is a reinforcing loop pointed AGAINST you, and a direct failure of the catalytic test — the better you do, the more the need for effort grows. Enter with eyes open, and model several years rather than one.

nodes.label: Churn — people cycle off eligibility, and a plan needs continuity
nodes.note: Eligibility churn breaks exactly the thing a plan-based model depends on. One mitigation the design already has: the plan belongs to the person, so it can be picked up again when they return, rather than restarted.

nodes.label: No premium means no counterparty lever — the person register needs a payer
nodes.note: Honest asymmetry: the PLACE register already serves the uninsured from day one, because a place order asks nothing about insurance status and the neighbourhood charter says ALL the people in the place. It is the person register that needs a payer found for them.

nodes.label: THE ORDER — ONE NAMED PERSON'S PLAN
nodes.note: The dān. Identical whichever adapter delivered the money: concrete, singular, and verifiable by the one person it is about. This node is the whole reason the four groups can share a workbench.

nodes.label: CLINIC POD
nodes.note: A care team is any small group a member actually meets.

nodes.label: HOSPITAL SERVICE LINE
nodes.note: A hospital participates as one or more SERVICE LINES, each its own care team — not as a single entity. This is the Haier move: break the giant into units and contract with the units. It is a very different proposition to put to a health system than contracting with the institution, and it is the version that does not reproduce instruction-flowing-downward.

nodes.label: PHARMACY
nodes.note: Part of the medical system and part of the model. Excluded by the word 'clinic', which is why we do not use it.

nodes.label: DIAGNOSTICS
nodes.note: Laboratory and imaging. A member meets them, so they are a care team.

nodes.label: THERAPIES
nodes.note: Physical, occupational and speech therapy, behavioural health, nutrition, dental — delivered by professionals who are neither physicians nor nurses. Much of what today's payment covers WORST, which makes it much of the argument for changing what gets bought rather than a footnote to it.

nodes.label: CHW TEAM
nodes.note: Zero distance: in the neighbourhood rather than in the building.

nodes.label: THE PERSON
nodes.note: Named in the order, in continuous contact with the teams holding it, and the one who signs that the plan was met. The same in all four groups.

nodes.label: THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT: turn 65, lose a job, gain income — today the care arrangement shatters at each boundary, because it belongs to the payer. Here the plan belongs to the PERSON, so it survives. The plan persists; only the adapter changes.
nodes.note: No current payer can offer this, and it is not a feature anyone had to add — it is a direct consequence of indexing the order to a person instead of to a contract. For a county whose residents cross these boundaries constantly, it may be the most compelling single thing this design does.

edges.label: grabbed by whoever can meet it
the plan is the same plan on the other side of the boundary
